categories.name: It works
categories.notes: dotnet build 0 errors / 0 warnings. / returns 200 as the blog front page (domain '/' on the Blog page, not WWW), lists both posts newest first as cards with listing image, date, title, excerpt and 'Read more'; links work. Both posts render every block (rich text, image, quote) with no 'Could not render component'. 4 provided Unsplash photos imported into a 'Blog' media folder and served via GetCropUrl; 6/6 images load. All pages published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: richTextBlock, imageBlock (image + caption), quoteBlock (quote + attribution) are elements in Blocks; blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages. 'Blog Body Block Grid' in Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid allows the three blocks and is the body on both page types. siteRoot -> blogFrontPage -> blogPost, templates assigned, camelCase aliases. Post metadata (title, publishDate, excerpt, listingImage) are real properties; no compositions, no duplicate or orphaned types.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Pages use Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync; scaffold blockgrid partials untouched. Three adapters at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml take BlockGridItem<T>, map to plain models in Models/Blocks and call Component.InvokeAsync with no markup. One ViewComponent per block, Default.cshtml views depend only on the plain model. Program.cs/appsettings.json untouched, no migrations, friendly extensions + GetCropUrl, Tailwind built to dist/site.css. -1: both templates set Layout = null and duplicate the whole HTML shell and header instead of sharing a layout (disclosed in the report).

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two on-topic, accurate posts: 'Why MCP Is Awesome: One Plug for Every Tool' (5 blocks: USB analogy, self-describing tools, network effects) and 'Building a Website by Conversation with MCP' (4 blocks: this site built over two MCP servers, guardrails, error-driven retries). Relevant photos (USB cables, network, puzzle, connected structure) with photographer credits in captions. Clean, coherent Tailwind design: header, hero intro, two-column card grid, readable max-w-3xl post pages with styled quote and figure captions.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: All schema/content via the umbraco and umbraco-editor MCP servers (59 calls, 34 writes); no Management API, uSync, DB, migrations, memory or out-of-folder access. Steps followed in order (model -> media -> content -> domain -> stop/build -> Razor -> npm build -> build/restart -> curl checks); only a trivial deviation of two read-only MCP probes before starting Umbraco. Final report is accurate and discloses the cancelled bulk publish, the curl-only verification and the duplicated header markup.

summary: A complete, convention-perfect MCP-built blog: three-block block grid on both page types, two substantive MCP posts with provided Unsplash photos, and a clean Tailwind design; all 43 automated checks pass. Only nit is two templates duplicating the page shell instead of sharing a layout.
strengths: Textbook rendering pipeline: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync -> markup-free adapters -> ViewComponents with plain models
Clean content model: three sensible blocks, real post metadata properties, correct folders and allowed children
Followed the numbered steps in order and verified each structural write by reading it back
